item: synthetic GPU memory: Gaussians and peak
content: Checkpoints (CPU, mmap): smoke synthetic A 76 keyframes -> 2.24 M Gaussians after the 30000-iteration refinement (the 09-30 5 Hz run without refinement had ~214 k at 10.8 s: densification x~10); smoke B 140 keyframes -> 3.18 M (2.70 M alive), sampled peak 15.5 / 16.3 GB at 87% of B's refinement (16 it/s). Real row 4 v2: A 209 keyframes -> 1.75 M (peak 14.7 GB), B 398 -> 0.88 M, C 818 -> 0.60 M (real refinement densifies ~x2 and the count falls across sessions). The relation of peak to Gaussians is not established from two points (image sizes differ: synthetic 680x480 at step 1, real 960x540); the full synthetic sessions have 3.9 x (A) and 4.6 x (B) the smoke's keyframes, so the refinement peak is expected above 16 GB.

No published GaME config is lighter: Aria room0/1 keyframe_translation_diff 0.01, keyframe_iters 200, refinement_iters 40000; TUM desk/office/xyz 0.05, 600, 40000; Flat 1.25 (x0.1 m), 50, 30000 is the lightest. GaME's densification (game.py:83-124 densify_and_prune) passes no cap (FlashSplat limit_num default -1): no published bound on the Gaussian count. So there is no published setting to switch to, and no number of ours is introduced.

item: synthetic GPU memory: what the queue does
content: queue13b (replaces queue13 at 19:53, nothing had started): synthetic rows run once each (run_once: no OOM rerun, a repeat OOM is predictable), with nvidia-smi every 10 s into <run>.vram.log; synthetic row 4 waits for syn_row4_commit.txt, written only after real row 4 v3 is judged. The first synthetic job is the measurement: OOM -> marked with its peak, the queue stops, the synthetic GaME rows are reported as infeasible on 16 GB with the published config (as Aria/TUM, feedback 2026-10-05), and the decision goes to the user; no own config change.
